title: Feature Ecosystem Stability and Contract Migration Playbook
author: Leah Kim
body:
Overview

## Objective
This playbook describes the process, criteria, and operational runbook for sunsetting, replacing, or materially changing feature variants and the associated commercial contracts (pricing, SLAs, entitlements) that customers rely on. It is intended to be used by Product, Sales, Legal, Solutions, and Engineering when executing migrations that affect runtime fidelity, pricing, or feature availability.

## Scope
- Includes: feature variant deprecations, major fidelity or quantization changes, bundle/sku consolidation, and any change that requires contract amendments (billing, SLAs, credits).
- Excludes: purely UI copy updates, minor telemetry label changes, or backend refactors that do not change customer-visible behavior or economics.

## Goals and success criteria
- Customer impact: <= 5% of active customers (by revenue) experience a functional regression during migration window.
- Quality SLO delta: no more than +3% error/regression rate on critical prompt-sets defined in the shadow-eval harness.
- Latency: 95th percentile latency change <= +15% for affected routes.
- Cost: customer-facing unit economics changes communicated and, where possible, limited to +/-10% unless explicitly negotiated.

## Roles and owners
- Feature Lead (Product): accountable for product decisions, migration schedule, and customer communications.
- Engineering Lead (Runtime): responsible for compatibility mapping, canary plan, and rollback hooks.
- Billing Owner (Finance): controls pricing deltas, credit calculation, and contract amendments.
- Legal/Compliance: approves contract language and special terms.
- Solutions/SE: customer facing runbook and migration execution support.

## Decision criteria for migration
Before proceeding, the following must be validated and documented:
1) Compatibility matrix between old and new variants (models, quantized profiles, runtime knobs).
2) Shadow-eval results for standard prompt-sets: pass threshold = mean quality delta <= 1.5 percentage points across top-3 metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/F1 or task-specific).
3) Cost delta simulation for expected traffic patterns; if delta > 10% for top-10 customers, prepare tailored commercial options.
4) Required contract changes identified and approved by Legal + Billing.

## Migration timeline (high level)
- T-minus 60 days: initiate cross-functional kickoff, identify affected customers, and assemble migration project.
- T-minus 45 days: complete compatibility matrix and run initial shadow evaluations.
- T-minus 30 days: finalize commercial options and draft customer notices.
- T-minus 14 days: start gated canary (internal + opt-in clients), open support channels and escalation playbook.
- T-minus 3 days: freeze non-critical changes to dependent services.
- Migration day (D): execute staged rollout with automated health gates.
- D+1 to D+30: monitoring, customer remediation, and follow-up reviews.

## Playbook: step-by-step
1) Identification and scoping
   - Produce a list of affected routes, customers (by entitlement SKU), and any downstream systems (analytics, billing).
   - Create a migration spreadsheet with columns: route, old_variant_id, new_variant_id, critical_prompts, expected_cost_delta, primary_contacts.

2) Compatibility mapping
   - Engineering to produce a compatibility matrix that maps model architecture, quantization profile, kernel/ops differences, and fallback paths.
   - Define automatic fallback policies: route->variant precedence, regional fallthrough, and emergency throttle.

3) Shadow evaluation and quality gates
   - Use the Eval Harness to run: unit prompt-sets, customer-provided prompts (where available), and long-tail fuzz tests.
   - Required thresholds: quality delta mean <= 1.5 percentage points, 99th percentile hallucination signal unchanged.

4) Commercial impact analysis and packaging
   - Finance simulates billing change per tenant for projected usage patterns (see sample billing delta table below).
   - If commercial delta > 10% for >5 customers or >20% for any single customer, product should prepare an opt-in grandfathering proposal (time-limited credits or variant pinning).

   Sample billing delta table (example):

   | Customer Tier | Typical Monthly Tokens | Old Unit Cost | New Unit Cost | Delta % | Recommended Remedy |
   |---------------|------------------------:|--------------:|--------------:|--------:|---------------------|
   | Startup       | 50M                    | $0.0012       | $0.00132      | +10%   | 3-month credit      |
   | Scale         | 500M                   | $0.0009       | $0.00097      | +7.8%  | Communicate & opt-in|
   | Enterprise    | 4B                     | $0.0007       | $0.00085      | +21.4% | Commercial review   |

5) Contract language and SLO amendments
   - Legal drafts amendment language with: migration window, rollback remedies, credit formula, and termination triggers.
   - SLO changes must include observability hooks: per-route latency/cost telemetry retention = 90 days and an SLA credit formula for availability/quality regressions.

6) Canary and rollout plan
   - Canary cohorts: internal dev cluster (1 day) -> opt-in customers (7–14 days) -> graduated public rollout (region-by-region).
   - Automated health gates evaluate: error rate, 95p latency, quality shadow-eval metrics, and billing anomalies. If any gate trips, rollback immediately to previous variant and open incident bridge.

7) Customer communications
   - Templates: 60-day notice, 30-day technical migration guide, and day-of migration reminder. Messages must include: timeline, impact summary, support contacts, and opt-out/pin options when available.

8) Release notes and internal runbook
   - Publish release notes that document: feature change summary, affected routes, API compatibility notes, migration window, and contact points. Internal runbook includes step-by-step rollback commands and scripts.

   Example Release Notes snippet:
   "As of 2029-07-01 we are migrating route /generate/tts from variant-a-quant to variant-b-compat. Impact: marginal latency increase for long conversations; recommended action: test on staging. Contact solutions@redwood.ai for pinning options."

## Rollback criteria and playbook
- Rollback triggers (any of the following during the migration window):
  * > +5% error rate vs baseline on production traffic for 30 minutes.
  * Quality gate failure on customer-provided prompt-sets.
  * Billing anomaly: unexpected > 15% immediate unit cost change for any active customer.
- Rollback steps:
  1. Open incident bridge and notify stakeholders.
  2. Execute automated variant switch to previous variant ID.
  3. Confirm shadow-eval run and run manual checklists for top-10 customers.
  4. Issue customer communications and apply credits if necessary.

## Metrics and monitoring
- Primary metrics to track (per-route and per-tenant where possible):
  * Request success rate (4xx/5xx), 1m/5m windows.
  * Latency p50/p90/p95.
  * Shadow-eval quality metrics (task-specific scores).
  * Billing/unit-cost deltas and token consumption patterns.
  * Customer support volume (tickets, severity).

- Dashboards to create prior to migration:
  1) Migration health overview (global): success rate, latency, quality score deltas.
  2) Top customers impact board: per-tenant cost delta and usage, contact info.
  3) Canary watch: per-cohort telemetry with automated alerting.

## Tooling and automation
- Provide a migration CLI for safe rollouts and rollbacks. Example usage:

  # dry-run compatibility report for route
  redwood-migrate plan --route /v1/generate/chat --from variant-a --to variant-b --dry-run
\  # execute staged rollout to 10%
  redwood-migrate rollout --route /v1/generate/chat --to variant-b --percent 10 --watch

- Automation responsibilities: Engineering to own scripts in runtime repo; Product to version migration plans and ensure billing overrides are property-flagged.

## Communication templates (brief)
- 60-day notice: high-level rationale, impact matrix, migration timeline, contact and opt-out options.
- 30-day technical guide: API compatibility notes, sample code to pin variants, and testing checklist.
- Day-of alert: short status + support bridge link.

## Post-migration review
- T+7 day review: collect telemetry, tickets, and run retrospective with cross-functional stakeholders.
- T+30 day commercial reconciliation: apply credits, finalize amendments, and publish final release notes.

## Appendix A — Variant pin sample API
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/customers/{tenant_id}/pin" \\
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \\
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \\
  -d '{"route": "/v1/generate/chat", "variant_id": "variant-a", "expire_at": "2029-12-01T00:00:00Z" }'
